definitions.explanation: A heavy outer garment worn over other clothing for warmth. A somewhat literary or old-fashioned word, now largely replaced by コート in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {外套|がいとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{羽織|はお}る→羽織る：13901_haoru⟧。
⟦{寒|さむ}さ→寒さ：12336_samusa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耐|た}え→耐える：12087_taeru⟧かねて{外套|がいとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{襟|えり}→襟：06487_eri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てた→立てる：01196_tateru⟧。
examples.english: Unable to bear the cold, he turned up the collar of his overcoat.
He picked up the black overcoat hanging in the entryway and went out into the night streets.

notes:
A literary compound of ⟦{外|がい}→外〜：03948_gai⟧ (outer) + {套|とう} (covering/sheath). More commonly encountered in literature, period dramas, and historical writing than in everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外套|がいとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧: to wear an overcoat
- {外套|がいとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧: to take off an overcoat
- {外套|がいとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{羽織|はお}る→羽織る：13901_haoru⟧: to throw on an overcoat
- {軍用|ぐんよう}{外套|がいとう}: military overcoat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦コート→コート：01358_kooto⟧: coat — the standard modern word for coats and overcoats
- ⟦オーバー→オーバー：01529_oobaa⟧: overcoat — older loanword (from 'overcoat'), still used by older speakers
- ⟦マント→マント：11267_manto⟧: mantle, cape — a cloak-style outer garment

LITERARY NOTE:
{外套|がいとう} is the Japanese title of Gogol's famous short story "The Overcoat." The word evokes a literary, atmospheric quality.
